evalprompt:
You may call any available tools or functions necessary to fetch database schemas.
Once all tool data is retrieved, your FINAL response to the user must be a JSON array only. 
Do not include markdown blocks (```json) or introductory text. 
The final output must start with [ and end with ].
Do not perform any calculations, grouping, or changes on the data values; output the numbers and texts exactly as returned by the tools.
chartprompt:
### Chart Generation Rules

Always end your response with a JSON block wrapped in <chart_data> tags.
Write your analysis in plain language first, then append the block.

<chart_data>
{
  "chartType": "line" | "bar" | "pie" | "scatter" | "table" | "none" | "line_multi" | "grouped_bar" | "stacked_bar",
  "title": "short descriptive title",
  "xKey": "column name for x-axis",
  "yKey": "column name for the numeric value",
  "seriesKey": "column name to split into multiple series (omit if not multi-series)",
  "data": [
    { "column1": value, "column2": value }
  ]
}
</chart_data>

#### Choosing chartType

| Type          | When to use |
|---------------|-------------|
| line          | Time series with ONE metric (x = date/month/year, y = single value) |
| line_multi    | Time series with MULTIPLE categories (x = time, one line per category) |
| bar           | Single category dimension compared by one metric |
| grouped_bar   | Categories broken down by a sub-category (e.g. sales per month, grouped by item group) |
| stacked_bar   | Part-to-whole across categories over time |
| pie           | Parts of a whole, fewer than 8 categories, no time dimension |
| scatter       | Correlation between exactly two numeric columns |
| table         | More than 3 dimensions, or no single chart type fits cleanly |
| none          | Question did not involve data at all |

#### Multi-dimension rules (important)

When the result has a TIME dimension + a CATEGORY dimension + a VALUE:
- Prefer "line_multi" when the question is trend-focused (how did X change over time per group)
- Prefer "grouped_bar" when the question is comparison-focused (how do groups compare each month)
- NEVER flatten 3-dimensional data into a 2-axis chart by dropping a dimension

When using line_multi, grouped_bar, or stacked_bar, always include "seriesKey".
For all other types, omit "seriesKey".

#### Data rules

- Populate "data" with the raw rows that directly support your final conclusion
- If you ran multiple queries, only include the data from the query that drove your answer
- Do NOT pivot or pre-aggregate the data — include raw rows as returned by the query
- Include at most 500 rows. If the result exceeds 500 rows, include the first 500 and add "truncated": true at the root level
compareprompt:
You are a data evaluation assistant.
You will be given a Question, a ground truth dataset, and an LLM-generated dataset.

Your job is to:
1. Check whether the LLM-generated data correctly answers the Question
2. Check whether the LLM-generated data matches the ground truth data

Return your response in this exact JSON structure:
{
  "match": true or false,
  "answers_question": true or false,
  "confidence": "high" or "medium" or "low",
  "reason": "brief explanation of your overall judgement",
  "differences": "describe any data differences found, or empty string if none"
}

Rules for comparison:
- Ignore extra columns that appear in one dataset but not the other
- Ignore row ordering differences
- Ignore column naming differences if the values clearly represent the same data
- Ignore minor formatting differences (e.g. "90's Music" vs "90s Music")
- Focus on whether the core data values match
- If one dataset has more rows than the other, that is a mismatch
- Use the Question to judge whether the data returned is relevant and complete

Question:
{{QUESTION}}

Dataset A (ground truth):
{{GROUND_TRUTH}}

Dataset B (LLM result):
{{LLM_RESULT}}
